item.title: Re: Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Confirming my permission here was granted.

As much fun as those images were, we have rules around these here parts.

item.title: Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded: The images used in this article are non-compliant with the SCP wiki's license (CC-BY-SA 3.0) as the first image came from here (all rights reserved), the second image's source is unknown and thus can be assumed to be non-compliant, and the third image is from this blog (with no indication it was released under creative commons). Thus, the images have been removed and the corresponding "Illustrations" section has been removed with Conwell's permission.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Finally got around to reading this, do not regret it. A really great example of the format, and a pitch-perfect setup for future exploration in tales. Good job all around, I look forward to seeing any continuations of this series!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Right — and Ways into the Library are often referred to as specifically as "Doors", as a subset of Ways — but I think that the author's intent was "these people are assuming/not assuming that any portal connected to the Library is a Way" not necessarily "Ways only connect to the Library"

Of course, I'm sure they'll correct me if I misread :)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Using Way only to refer to ways to and from the library is a way more restrictive definition than is usually seen. At least in WL tales/articles it is fairly commonly used to refer to portals between worlds other than earth or the library.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This is really good, evocative, charming, and fertile ground for further stories. I especially like the set-up of the key being something non-obvious in the local environment.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Glad you think so. Truth be told that part came at the recommendation of the deadlymoose. Had I known it would have been popular I might have included more footnote debates.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think my favorite part was the footnotes consisting of two researchers arguing over what exactly constitutes a Way. It seems so… academic. :)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Glad you liked this TL. Feel free to send me a PM with anything you caught on your read through if you are so inclined. Additionally, your spelling recommendation has been included.

item.title: Author's Post
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so this is the GoI Format for Team Wayfarer (Eta-13) in the MTF Contest. First time making an GoI format article, but this was fun to make, so I might try my hand at it again in the future.

Special thanks to my teammates, DreamwalkerFae and kol aumer, for all their help shaping this.

Additional thanks to: Crayne, Metaphysician, minmin, Thekillerax, TwistedGears, thedeadlymoose, Randomini, MacLeod, Von Pincier, and djkaktus. All of whom took a look at this when it was a draft and provided a plethora of much needed feedback.

Hope you guys enjoy.

Conwell
